title: Quasi-compact opens of a directed limit of spectral spaces descend to a finite stage
statement: Let $I$ be a directed set (nonempty, any two elements have a common upper bound), let $(X_i)_{i\in I}$ be spectral spaces [def-weil-spectral-space] and for $i\le i'$ let $f_{ii'}:X_{i'}\to X_i$ be spectral maps (continuous, with $f_{ii'}^{-1}(W)$ quasi-compact for every quasi-compact open $W\subseteq X_i$), with $f_{ii}=\mathrm{id}$ and $f_{ii'}\circ f_{i'i''}=f_{ii''}$ for $i\le i'\le i''$. Let $X$ be a topological space with continuous maps $p_i:X\to X_i$, $f_{ii'}\circ p_{i'}=p_i$, which is a limit of the system in the category of topological spaces (the map $x\mapsto(p_i(x))_i$ is a bijection of $X$ onto $\{(x_i)\in\prod_iX_i: f_{ii'}(x_{i'})=x_i\text{ for }i\le i'\}$ and the topology of $X$ is the coarsest for which all $p_i$ are continuous). Then: (1) for every quasi-compact open $U\subseteq X$ there are $i\in I$ and a quasi-compact open $U_i\subseteq X_i$ with $p_i^{-1}(U_i)=U$; (2) if $U_i\subseteq X_i$, $U_j\subseteq X_j$ are quasi-compact opens with $p_i^{-1}(U_i)\subseteq p_j^{-1}(U_j)$, there is $k\in I$ with $k\ge i,j$ and $f_{ik}^{-1}(U_i)\subseteq f_{jk}^{-1}(U_j)$; (3) if $U_i,U_{1,i},\dots,U_{n,i}\subseteq X_i$ are quasi-compact opens with $p_i^{-1}(U_i)=\bigcup_lp_i^{-1}(U_{l,i})$, then $f_{ii'}^{-1}(U_i)=\bigcup_lf_{ii'}^{-1}(U_{l,i})$ for some $i'\ge i$; (4) the same as (3) with intersections in place of unions.

source.place: Topology, Lemma Tag 0A30 (label lemma-descend-opens, line 4969), stated there for a cofiltered index category; a directed set is the special case used here

proof.text: *Step 1 (a basis of quasi-compact opens pulled back from the stages).* Let $\mathcal B$ be the set of subsets of $X$ of the form $p_i^{-1}(W)$ with $i\in I$ and $W\subseteq X_i$ a quasi-compact open. (a) Let $B_l=p_{i_l}^{-1}(W_l)\in\mathcal B$, $l=1,\dots,r$ ($r\ge0$), and let $k\in I$ with $k\ge i_1,\dots,i_r$ (it exists since $I$ is nonempty and directed). As $p_{i_l}=f_{i_lk}\circ p_k$ we have $B_l=p_k^{-1}(W'_l)$ with $W'_l=f_{i_lk}^{-1}(W_l)$, which is a quasi-compact open of $X_k$ because $f_{i_lk}$ is spectral. Hence $B_1\cup\dots\cup B_r=p_k^{-1}(W'_1\cup\dots\cup W'_r)$ and $B_1\cap\dots\cap B_r=p_k^{-1}(W'_1\cap\dots\cap W'_r)$ (for $r=0$: $\emptyset=p_k^{-1}(\emptyset)$ and $X=p_k^{-1}(X_k)$). A finite union of quasi-compact opens is a quasi-compact open; a finite intersection of quasi-compact opens of the spectral space $X_k$ is a quasi-compact open, since $X_k$ is quasi-compact and the intersection of two quasi-compact opens of $X_k$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-spectral-space]. So $\mathcal B$ is closed under finite unions and finite intersections. (b) $\mathcal B$ is a basis of the topology of $X$: its members are open since the $p_i$ are continuous; conversely the topology of $X$ is the coarsest for which all $p_i$ are continuous, so every open of $X$ is a union of finite intersections of sets $p_i^{-1}(V)$, $V\subseteq X_i$ open. Each $p_i^{-1}(V)$ is the union of the $p_i^{-1}(W)$ over the quasi-compact opens $W\subseteq V$, since these $W$ cover $V$ (the quasi-compact opens form a basis of $X_i$ [def-weil-spectral-space]); distributing, a finite intersection of such unions is a union of finite intersections of members of $\mathcal B$, which lie in $\mathcal B$ by (a). Hence every open of $X$ is a union of members of $\mathcal B$.

source.place: Topology, proof of Lemma Tag 0A2Z (label lemma-directed-inverse-limit-spectral-spaces, line 4902), second paragraph (a basis of X is given by the p_i^{-1}(U_i) with U_i quasi-compact open), which rests on Lemma Tag 0A2P (label lemma-describe-limits, line 2374); for a directed set and the explicit limit topology of the statement this is the definition, written out here

proof.text: *Step 2 (part (1)).* Let $U\subseteq X$ be a quasi-compact open. By Step 1 (b), $U$ is the union of the members of $\mathcal B$ contained in $U$; as $U$ is quasi-compact, finitely many of them, $B_1,\dots,B_r$, already cover $U$, so $U=B_1\cup\dots\cup B_r$. By Step 1 (a) this union lies in $\mathcal B$: $U=p_k^{-1}(U_k)$ for some $k\in I$ and some quasi-compact open $U_k\subseteq X_k$. This is (1) (with $i=k$).

source.place: Topology, proof of Lemma Tag 0A30 (label lemma-descend-opens, line 4969): '(1) is a special case of Lemma 0A2Y'; proof of Lemma Tag 0A2Y (label lemma-inverse-limit-spectral-spaces-constructible, line 4862), first paragraph (write E = p_i^{-1}(U_i), cover U_i by quasi-compact opens, use the quasi-compactness of E)

proof.text: *Step 3 (part (2): the sets $Z_k$).* Let $U_i\subseteq X_i$, $U_j\subseteq X_j$ be quasi-compact opens with $p_i^{-1}(U_i)\subseteq p_j^{-1}(U_j)$. Choose $k_0\in I$ with $k_0\ge i,j$ and let $K=\{k\in I:k\ge k_0\}$; $K$ is a directed set ($k_0\in K$, and an upper bound in $I$ of two elements of $K$ lies in $K$). For $k\in K$ put $A_k=f_{ik}^{-1}(U_i)$ and $B_k=f_{jk}^{-1}(U_j)$, quasi-compact opens of $X_k$ (the $f$'s are spectral), and $Z_k=A_k\setminus B_k=A_k\cap(X_k\setminus B_k)$. In the constructible topology of $X_k$ every quasi-compact open of $X_k$ is both open and closed [def-weil-pbc-constructible-topology]; so $A_k$ is closed in it, and $X_k\setminus B_k$, the complement of the open $B_k$, is closed in it; hence $Z_k$ is closed in the constructible topology of $X_k$. For $k\le k'$ in $K$ we have $f_{ik'}=f_{ik}\circ f_{kk'}$ and $f_{jk'}=f_{jk}\circ f_{kk'}$, hence $A_{k'}=f_{kk'}^{-1}(A_k)$, $B_{k'}=f_{kk'}^{-1}(B_k)$ and $Z_{k'}=f_{kk'}^{-1}(Z_k)$; in particular $f_{kk'}(Z_{k'})\subseteq Z_k$.

source.place: Topology, proof of Lemma Tag 0A2X (label lemma-inverse-limit-spectral-spaces-equal, line 4836), with E = U_i closed and F = U_j open in the constructible topology, as in the proof of Lemma Tag 0A30 (2) ('quasi-compact opens are both open and closed in the constructible topology'); the two indices i, j are brought to the common stage k_0 here

proof.text: *Step 4 (part (2): some $Z_k$ is empty).* We claim $Z_k=\emptyset$ for some $k\in K$; then $k\ge i,j$ and $A_k\subseteq B_k$, i.e. $f_{ik}^{-1}(U_i)\subseteq f_{jk}^{-1}(U_j)$, which is (2). Suppose instead that every $Z_k$, $k\in K$, is nonempty. The directed set $K$, the spectral spaces $X_k$ ($k\in K$) with the spectral maps $f_{kk'}$ ($k\le k'$ in $K$), and the nonempty subsets $Z_k$, closed in the constructible topology with $f_{kk'}(Z_{k'})\subseteq Z_k$ (Step 3), satisfy the hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-spectral-limit-constructible-closed-nonempty], which gives $z_k\in Z_k$ ($k\in K$) with $f_{kk'}(z_{k'})=z_k$ for $k\le k'$ in $K$. Extend this to all of $I$: for $l\in I$ choose $k\in K$ with $k\ge l$ and put $x_l=f_{lk}(z_k)$. This does not depend on $k$: for two choices $k,k'$ take $k''\in K$ above both, then $f_{lk}(z_k)=f_{lk}(f_{kk''}(z_{k''}))=f_{lk''}(z_{k''})$ and likewise for $k'$. For $l\in K$, taking $k=l$ gives $x_l=z_l$. For $l\le l'$ in $I$, with $k\in K$, $k\ge l'$: $f_{ll'}(x_{l'})=f_{ll'}(f_{l'k}(z_k))=f_{lk}(z_k)=x_l$. By the description of $X$ in the statement there is $x\in X$ with $p_l(x)=x_l$ for all $l\in I$. Then $p_i(x)=x_i=f_{ik_0}(z_{k_0})\in U_i$ because $z_{k_0}\in A_{k_0}$, so $x\in p_i^{-1}(U_i)\subseteq p_j^{-1}(U_j)$; but $p_j(x)=f_{jk_0}(z_{k_0})\notin U_j$ because $z_{k_0}\notin B_{k_0}$. This contradiction proves the claim.

source.place: Topology, proof of Lemma Tag 0A2X (label lemma-inverse-limit-spectral-spaces-equal, line 4836): p_i^{-1}(E) minus p_i^{-1}(F) is the limit of the sets f_a^{-1}(E) minus f_a^{-1}(F), which is nonempty if each of them is by Lemma Tag 0A2W (label lemma-inverse-limit-spectral-spaces-nonempty, line 4810) (1); the identification of a compatible family over K with a point of X (K cofinal in I) is written out here

proof.text: *Step 5 (parts (3) and (4)).* Let $U_i,U_{1,i},\dots,U_{n,i}\subseteq X_i$ be quasi-compact opens and let $V=U_{1,i}\cup\dots\cup U_{n,i}$ for (3), resp. $V=U_{1,i}\cap\dots\cap U_{n,i}$ (with $V=X_i$ for $n=0$) for (4). $V$ is a quasi-compact open of $X_i$: a finite union of quasi-compact opens is one, and so is a finite intersection in the spectral space $X_i$ ($X_i$ is quasi-compact and the intersection of two quasi-compact opens is quasi-compact [def-weil-spectral-space]). Preimages commute with unions and intersections, so the hypothesis says $p_i^{-1}(U_i)=p_i^{-1}(V)$, and the conclusion to be shown is $f_{ii'}^{-1}(U_i)=f_{ii'}^{-1}(V)$ for some $i'\ge i$. By (2) (Steps 3 and 4, with $j=i$) applied to $p_i^{-1}(U_i)\subseteq p_i^{-1}(V)$ there is $k\ge i$ with $f_{ik}^{-1}(U_i)\subseteq f_{ik}^{-1}(V)$, and applied to $p_i^{-1}(V)\subseteq p_i^{-1}(U_i)$ there is $k'\ge i$ with $f_{ik'}^{-1}(V)\subseteq f_{ik'}^{-1}(U_i)$. Choose $i'\ge k,k'$. Taking preimages under $f_{ki'}$ and using $f_{ii'}=f_{ik}\circ f_{ki'}$ gives $f_{ii'}^{-1}(U_i)\subseteq f_{ii'}^{-1}(V)$; likewise with $f_{k'i'}$ gives $f_{ii'}^{-1}(V)\subseteq f_{ii'}^{-1}(U_i)$. Hence $f_{ii'}^{-1}(U_i)=f_{ii'}^{-1}(V)$, which is $\bigcup_lf_{ii'}^{-1}(U_{l,i})$ in case (3) and $\bigcap_lf_{ii'}^{-1}(U_{l,i})$ in case (4).
